ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, notably by the Law of 13 February 2018 transposing the 4th and 5th EU AML Directives; Law of 13 January 2019 and Law of 25 March 2020 establishing and governing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2018 on the identification of beneficial owners. Under these instruments, direct or indirect ownership of more than 25% of shares, voting rights, or control by other means constitutes beneficial ownership. A Luxembourg notary and the opening credit institution must conduct full KYC/CDD on the shareholders, managers, and ultimate beneficial owners before incorporation, and the entity must file its UBO particulars with the RBE within one month of incorporation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statuts) drafted and executed as an authentic notarial deed of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg civil-law notary, member of the Chamber of Notaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic authentic act; no apostille required; deposited with the Luxembourg Business Registers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of each shareholder, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the country of origin (passport office, national civil registry, or consular authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the country of origin is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each shareholder, manager, and UBO (recent utility bill or official certificate of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal registry or utility provider in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or certified translation by a sworn translator where the document is not in French, German, or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incorporation for any corporate shareholder or intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the intermediary entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter together with the certificate of blocking of funds evidencing payment of the EUR 12,000 statutory minimum share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution licensed by the CSSF and holding the blocked account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank instrument signed by authorized bank officers; no apostille required, but subject to the bank's independent AML/KYC acceptance procedures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation where the incorporator acts through a representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or competent notarial authority in the country of the grantor's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed abroad; domestic notarization if executed in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Manager's curriculum vitae and sworn declaration of no disqualification (fit-and-proper statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed manager of the SARL, authenticated by signature before a Luxembourg notary or sworn translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature authentication by notary or sworn translator; apostille not generally required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, managers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the Luxembourg national restrictive-measures list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, the OFAC SDN list for USD-denominated payment rails, and FATF public statements. Politically Exposed Persons must be identified using the CSSF and FATF PEP indicators and are subject to enhanced due diligence, including senior-management approval, verification of source of wealth and source of funds, and reinforced ongoing monitoring. CDD information must be refreshed at least every three years and upon any material change in ownership or control; the notary and the bank must document all screening results in the AML/CFT file before completion of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — www.lbr.lu, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL must bear a name that is lawful, distinctive, and not liable to create confusion with existing registered names. The name may be drafted in any language provided it is written in Latin characters and, where necessary, transliterated into Latin script; documents filed with the RCS are habitually drafted in French. The name must include the legal-form indicator 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the commonly used abbreviation 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.' and must not consist exclusively of generic or misleading geographical or activity terms.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SICAF / OPCVM / AIF
Luxembourg / État / State / National / Gouvernement / Commune / Municipal
Chambre de Commerce / Ministère / Ministry / Police / Armée / Croix-Rouge / Université
Avocat / Law Firm / Notaire / Cabinet d'Avocats
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a name reservation or registration by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant may: (1) file a written reconsideration request with LBR within one month of the refusal decision, attaching amended name proposals, evidence of distinctiveness, or authorizations from the competent minister or professional chamber where a sensitive token is involved; (2) if the reconsideration is denied, lodge an administrative appeal before the Tribunal administratif de Luxembourg within three months of the denial, pleading legal error, manifest error of assessment, or excess of power; (3) alternatively, where the refusal is grounded on a conflicting prior right, bring proceedings before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg in commercial matters; and (4) simultaneously submit a new name reservation with a reformed distinctive name. The appeal does not automatically suspend the refusal unless an interim-relief order is granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office consisting only of a PO Box or a non-existent physical location is not permissible. Luxembourg law requires the SARL to maintain a real and determinant registered office ('siège social') within the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. For an e-commerce IoT hardware retail entity, the use of a licensed domiciliation agent ('bureau de domiciliation') with a physical Luxembourg address is accepted, provided the company keeps its statutory books, corporate records, and management accessibility at that address and does not create a mere letterbox arrangement. Banks and payment processors such as Stripe and Shopify Payments will ordinarily require a verifiable physical address and may independently verify the substance of the registered office; the Luxembourg tax administration may apply abuse-of-law and substance doctrines if the office is purely artificial.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this industry classification: estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the RCS or competent public authority is approximately 5% for a low-risk, non-licensed retail SARL using its own leased office or a reputable domiciliation agent. The probability increases to approximately 15% if the company operates with a domiciliation-only address, if AML/CFT anomalies are flagged to the CSSF or the Financial Intelligence Unit, or if tax audit triggers are present. No routine proactive physical inspection regime applies to this ISIC class.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory minimum share capital deposited with a Luxembourg credit institution as a blocked account prior to incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum of EUR 12,000 fully subscribed and paid up under Article 710-1 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting, authentication, and signature of the notarial deed of incorporation (Articles of Association)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff fixed by Grand-Ducal regulation and prevailing market rate (EUR 1,500 - 2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, designated court, or consular office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document tariff under the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961; USD 150 average per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / commercial domiciliation service with physical Luxembourg address and mail handling, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate services provider or domiciliation agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC compliance setup: UBO risk assessment, PEP and sanctions screening repository, and CDD file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg legal counsel or independent AML consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk retail entity (EUR 1,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Fixed-fee legal counsel for incorporation, by-laws, corporate governance framework, and shareholder resolutions
Certified translations, courier, and incidental administrative costs for foreign-language documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended – Articles 180 et seq. (SARL regime); Law of 23 September 2020 on digitalisation of the Trade and Companies Register; Law of 14 December 2022 on modernisation of corporate law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg, with mandatory e-filing via the LBRonline portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg civil-law notary and filed electronically with the RCS; legal effect against third parties upon publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000 (each share minimum EUR 1.00); 100% of the subscribed capital must be deposited into a blocked account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution before notarization; the deposit is released only upon production of the RCS registration certificate – no separate state escrow account applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned sole shareholder of [●] S.à r.l. (the 'Company') ratifies the notarial deed of incorporation, the subscription of the entire share capital of EUR 12,000 divided into 120 fully paid-up shares of EUR 100 each, and the adoption of the registered office at [●], Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [●] shall be appointed Sole Manager (Gérant) of the Company with full powers to operate bank accounts, bind the Company, appoint auditors when required, and complete all filings with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and the RESA. RESOLVED FURTHERLY, that the articles of association take full effect as of the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBRonline
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-clearance request through a Luxembourg notary or directly via LBRonline; verify absence of conflicting registered names and trademarks for retail trade of electronic devices; obtain a Certificat de non-conflit de dénomination confirming availability of the proposed corporate name; reserve the name pending notarization.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copy of the sole shareholder and the proposed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses the name as confusingly similar or contrary to public order, the notary files an alternative name proposal or a justified rectification within the portal; trademark oppositions are cured by adopting a distinct secondary name variant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and pre-execution review of the articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Notaire) with seat in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to draft the statuts covering corporate name, municipality of registered office, corporate object (online retail of smart-home IoT hardware and home-automation systems, ISIC 4791), share capital structure, duration, and appointment of the first manager; the notary performs a legal-admissibility review before scheduling execution of the authentic deed.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of shareholder and manager
Proof of residential address of the manager
Consent letter of the appointed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies identified in the notary's legal review are corrected via drafting amendments or a supplemental rider (avenant) prior to execution; post-execution drafting errors are rectified by a separate notarial rectification deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital in blocked bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution licensed by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company to be formed; transfer the fully paid-up minimum share capital of EUR 12,000; the bank issues an attestation de blocage confirming the deposit and undertaking to release funds only against the RCS registration certificate; deliver the attestation to the notary before signature of the deed.
required_dossiers: Source-of-funds declaration under the AML Law of 12 November 2004
Brief business plan or corporate-object description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence or declines the file, the founders apply to another licensed Luxembourg credit institution; additional source-of-funds evidence is furnished to satisfy CSSF AML expectations before the blocked account is opened.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed and electronic RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and the RCS via LBRonline e-file submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary verifies the blocking certificate and legal admissibility, then executes the authentic deed of incorporation before the parties; within one business day thereafter, the notary transmits the deed and annexes to the RCS through LBRonline; the RCS assigns the registration number and issues the registration extract confirming legal personality.
required_dossiers: Declaration on honour of the manager (no conviction, no bankruptcy)
Proof of availability of registered office (lease or landlord consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a completeness query (demande de complément), the notary answers through the portal within the stated deadline and re-submits the corrected file without reopening the deed unless substantive changes are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA (electronic collection of companies and associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA publication service, Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, upload the executed articles of incorporation to the RESA for mandatory publication; pay the electronic publication fee (EUR 19 per deed); the RESA excerpt constitutes official proof of incorporation and establishes third-party effectiveness from the publication date.
required_dossiers: RCS-filed copy of the articles of incorporation
Electronic payment confirmation of the publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA portal rejects the submission due to formatting discrepancies, cure by re-uploading a compliant PDF version and verify the publication date to ensure that the succession of corporate steps remains legally uninterrupted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and operational post-incorporation registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number for e-commerce and distance sales (B2C platforms – Stripe and Shopify Payments); register the company with the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; enrol with the CCSS for employee social security if staff are hired; confirm that no autorisation d'établissement is required for online retailing of IoT hardware, while ensuring CE marking, RED/EMC compliance and data-protection obligations for payment processing.
required_dossiers: Identification of the effective place of management and Luxembourg bank account details
Commercial lease and, if applicable, fire and structural clearance for storage premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays VAT registration beyond the statutory window, file a formal follow-up and, if necessary, obtain a provisional VAT number; unresolved ACD registrations are escalated to the directorate, and taxable transactions are nonetheless declared on a best-efforts basis pending issuance of the definitive number.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate-General for Industry, with ILNAS (Luxembourg Institute for Standardization, Accreditation, Safety and Quality of Products and Services) responsible for market surveillance and conformity assessment of smart-home IoT radio equipment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No establishment license (autorisation d'établissement) is required for non-regulated online retailing of smart-home IoT hardware; a mandatory EU Declaration of Conformity with CE marking under Directive 2014/53/EU (Radio Equipment Directive) and Directive 2014/30/EU (electromagnetic compatibility) applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency) within the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category D (no EIA compulsory) for pure e-commerce warehousing and retailing of IoT devices without manufacturing or chemical processes; a simplified registration may be triggered if stored lithium-ion batteries exceed 60 kWh total installed capacity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions; compliance with municipal sewage discharge standards and the Grand-Ducal Regulation on water protection; WEEE registration and e-waste take-back obligations under Directive 2012/19/EU; RoHS substance restrictions under Directive 2011/65/EU; packaging waste compliance via the Valorlux/CONSOREM packaging schemes under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Fire and Rescue Service (Service d'incendie et de secours – SIS) for the registered office and any storage site; structural load inspection certificate for warehouse racking systems; workplace occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) confirming compliance with the Labour Code and the Law of 17 June 1994 on health and safety at work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDTVA) for value added tax; unified official filing and management portal: MyGuichet.lu; employer/income tax e-filing portal: e-Tax (offer.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident SARL, the statutory business identification number (Numéro d'identification national, 'matricule') is issued automatically upon incorporation through the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); the matricule forms the basis of the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format 'LU' + 8 digits) and the corporate income tax reference, with subsequent notification from the ACD/AEDTVA requiring no separate application. For non-resident foreign entities, the SOP is: (1) submit a VAT registration application to the AEDTVA (electronically via MyGuichet.lu or on prescribed paper form) attaching the RCS/foreign registry extract, evidence of an economic presence or a Luxembourg permanent establishment where required, and, when the foreign entity has no establishment in Luxembourg but performs taxable distance sales or imports into Luxembourg, documentation appointing a Luxembourg fiscal representative or confirmation of eligibility under the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme; (2) upon approval, receive the LU VAT identification number enabling EC Sales Listing, Intrastat filings, and import VAT accounting; (3) where a non-resident company holds a Luxembourg permanent establishment, additionally register with the ACD via a declaration of permanent establishment and appoint a local tax representative for corporate income tax and municipal business tax filings. Resident SARLs are automatically tax-registered; no further TIN procurement step is necessary beyond RCS formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg operates a classical entity-level corporate tax system with no US-style check-the-box election. Available elections and options include: (1) election for fiscal unity (tax consolidation) among a Luxembourg resident parent and its 95%-or-more held Luxembourg subsidiary companies (Article 164bis LIR), permitting offset of profits and losses within the group; (2) participation exemption election under Article 166 LIR exempting qualifying dividend income and capital gains; (3) intellectual property box election under Article 50quater LIR providing an 80% exemption on qualifying net IP income; (4) ATAD hybrid mismatch elections and the associated transitional grandfathering positions for legacy hybrid instruments; (5) optional renunciation of the small-business VAT franchise so as to remain in the normal VAT regime; and (6) election to constitute a VAT group (assujetti unique) among closely linked Luxembourg taxable persons.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, 'TVA') — EU-harmonised VAT pursuant to Council Directive 2006/112/EC and the Luxembourg Loi du 12 février 1979 relative à la TVA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business franchise exemption; mandatory VAT registration applies once annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or upon voluntary waiver of the franchise. Foreign suppliers making intra-EU distance sales of IoT hardware into Luxembourg must register once cross-border distance sales to non-taxable customers exceed the EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual threshold, except where the destination-country OSS registration is used. Imports of IoT hardware from non-EU countries into Luxembourg trigger import VAT registration and declaration obligations regardless of the franchised turnover threshold. Luxembourg applies the EU EUR 100,000 distance-sales threshold for sales from other EU member states where the seller does not possess an establishment in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no general real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital-stamping regime on ordinary B2B/B2C invoicing. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies to B2G contracts: suppliers must transmit structured e-invoices (EN 16931 / PEPPOL UBL or CII format) to Luxembourg public contracting authorities through a certified PEPPOL access point; there is no central government clearance API. For B2B and B2C invoices, electronic issuance is lawful subject to buyer consent and to guarantees preserving authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility; the AEDTVA recognises standardised e-invoicing formats, summary invoicing, and archival within Luxembourg or EEA cloud storage. No advance authorisation or digital stamp is required for VAT invoice numbering or for application of the 0% export rate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT is available for: (1) exports of goods — including smart-home IoT hardware — physically transported out of Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union (Article 43 Loi TVA), provided the export is supported by conclusive proof of dispatch/transport and the goods leave the EU within the statutory 90-day period from the supply; (2) intra-Community supplies to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number, where the supplier fulfils the EC Sales Listing and recapitulative statement duties (Article 42 Loi TVA); and (3) services directly connected with exported goods and supplied to non-EU recipients where the place of supply is outside the EU. For IoT hardware sold via Stripe or Shopify Payments, the 0% rate is denied unless per-parcel evidence documents the physical exit of each consignment: carrier tracking data, delivery address outside the EU, customs export declaration receipts, and sales contract/payment documentation matching the exporter of record.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Luxembourg Customs Export Declaration filed through the national electronic customs platform (NCTS / Single Administrative Document), evidencing acceptance and exit certification from the customs authority
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note showing transport of the goods from Luxembourg to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank MT103/payment-rail settlement records (Stripe/Shopify Payments payout logs) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the SARL's Luxembourg bank account
Commercial invoice and signed sales contract/purchase order identifying the exporter, foreign buyer, incoterms, and product description
Customs exit confirmation message or equivalent proof of physical exit of the goods from EU customs territory
Warehouse dispatch records, inventory movement report, and authorised warehousekeeper certificate where export stock is held in Luxembourg
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDTVA subjects export zero-rating claims to rigorous document-based audit, routinely cross-checking the customs exit certification against transport contracts, payment receipts, and warehouse records within a three-year assessment window, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or deliberate concealment. Failure to maintain or produce the mandatory substantiation triggers reassessment of output VAT at the 17% standard rate plus statutory default interest, and any input VAT recovered in reliance on the zero-rated export is clawed back. Administrative fines ranging from EUR 750 to EUR 1,500 per false or incomplete declaration are imposed under the Loi TVA penalty provisions. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, falsified export documentation, or fictitious export schemes constitute criminal tax fraud, punishable by substantial monetary penalties, custodial sentences under Luxembourg criminal law, forfeiture of export/Oss registration privileges, customs enforcement action, and enhanced exchange-of-information scrutiny under EU and OECD mutual assistance instruments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and the ECB Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM), jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT and financial-sector supervision. No separate foreign-exchange administration exists in Luxembourg; exchange-rate policy is euro-area competence, and the BCL operates TARGET2-LUX. The Luxembourg Ministry of Finance's financial-sanctions unit enforces EU/UN asset freezes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully liberalised under Articles 63-66 TFEU. There are no exchange-control approvals, quantitative limits, licensing regimes or convertibility barriers for trade settlements, dividends, loan repayments or equity capital flows. Profit remittance by a Luxembourg SARL is unrestricted, subject only to the 1915 Companies Law distribution/balance-sheet test, corporate tax filings and EU sanctions screening. Residual friction is limited to AML/KYC documentation (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02), the beneficial-owner register (Law of 13 January 2019) and sanctions-related due diligence on non-EEA counterparty banks. Invoicing may be freely denominated in EUR or any other convertible currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation window or mandatory conversion ratio for export/trading receipts. The SARL may freely retain EUR, USD or other currency balances in Luxembourg or EU bank accounts. For balance-of-payments statistics, each cross-border transfer must be tagged with the BCL/ECB purpose code; the servicing bank normally discharges this reporting obligation on behalf of the entity, but the BCL may require direct external-statistics reporting if annual cross-border payment flows are material or on specific request. No conversion obligation exists under any statutory timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR) with multi-currency sub-accounts (USD/GBP/CHF) and SEPA/SWIFT rails
Operational Account and blocked capital-escrow account ('compte de consignation') for SARL en formation
Remote-friendly operational account (EUR) for SME and e-commerce clients

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account (EUR) with conservative merchant-account policy
Operational account (EUR) for cooperatives and local SMEs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as a secondary treasury rail; do not use as primary bank. Luxembourg-licensed and EU-passported EMIs under PSD2 (EU 2015/2366) and the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business, Qonto) offer multi-currency virtual IBANs and cheaper FX conversion for Stripe/Shopify USD and GBP collections. Legal constraints: (i) EMI balances are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (FGDL) and are safeguarded, not lent; (ii) Luxembourg Tier-1 banks may treat EMI inflows as higher-risk and request source confirmation; (iii) EMIs cannot provide credit, overdrafts or documentary trade finance; and (iv) EMI AML/CFT files do not satisfy the notary or the formation bank for inbound capital validation. Blueprint: hold 1-3 weeks of working liquidity in a regulated EMI for FX efficiency, sweep residual balances daily to the BIL/BCEE operating account, and keep all equity and trade-finance flows at the Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or video-verified identification of at least one authorised signatory (manager and/or UBO) is required under CSSF Regulation 12-02. Remote opening is generally permitted for EEA-resident directors at ING Luxembourg and, in part, at BIL via certified video KYC, but the default rule for non-resident directors is a face-to-face interview at the bank counter or a notarised/apostilled identity certification by a Luxembourg notary. The bank always requires the RBE registration extract, articles of association, managers' resolution appointing bank correspondents, and a full UBO declaration. Account opening for an active e-commerce SARL typically takes 3-8 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or shareholders domiciled in third-country or higher-risk jurisdictions; bank demands source-of-wealth evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and proof of residential address (<3 months), bank reference letter from the UBO's primary bank, CV and business-activity narrative, corporate group organigram, RBE extract from the Luxembourg register, notarised source-of-funds declaration, and audited financial statements of any corporate parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume card-not-present receivables via Stripe and Shopify Payments, perceived as aggregated third-party funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe/Shopify merchant statements, PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance (AOC) for the SARL's e-commerce environment, refund and chargeback policy with <0.5% chargeback ratio, logistics/delivery evidence (courier reports or bills of lading), 12-month revenue forecast, business plan, and a signed representation that platform payouts represent genuine retail sales only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to contract manufacturers in China or Hong Kong triggering sanctions screening and payee KYC hurdles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice, purchase order, Incoterms contract (EXW/FOB), transport documents (MAWB/house airway bill), supplier incorporation certificate and bank account certificate, EU consolidated sanctions-list screening result, completed supplier KYC questionnaire, and HS tariff classification for each IoT hardware SKU.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital subscription in cash or via third-party financing; bank blocks release of the formation escrow account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of association evidencing the subscribed capital (minimum EUR 12,394.68), deposit receipt issued by the notary or Caisse de Consignation, shareholder payment records, source-of-funds statements of each subscriber, and a written declaration under Article 710-13 of the 1915 Companies Law that the capital is fully paid in.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: At formation, the full SARL stated capital (minimum EUR 12,394.68) must be paid in cash into a blocked 'SARL en formation' escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution or lodged with the notary before execution of the notarial deed; the bank releases the funds only upon RCS registration. Shareholder wires must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA if EEA) with the BPM6 purpose code 'equity - shares and other equity' (direct investment) and the company name, notary reference and subscription allocation in remittance information. The bank issues a release letter to the notary upon final credit. For subsequent capital increases, a notarised deed and RCS re-registration are required; each subscriber's wire must exactly match the notarial deed, the updated RBE extract and the UBO file. A dual-account structure is recommended: a zero-balance blocked capital account and a live EUR operating account, with all movements recorded in annual accounts to avoid Luxembourg CAMT inconsistencies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For non-EEA suppliers, settle via SWIFT MT103 (USD/CNY) with full remittance data including purpose code, purchase order and invoice number; for EEA suppliers, use SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.03) or Instant SEPA through TARGET2-LUX. For large initial IoT hardware orders, open an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600) via BIL/BCEE with 30-90 days tenor, or a Bank Payment Obligation under ICC URBPO; where advance payment is required, obtain a standby LC or advance-payment guarantee from the supplier's bank. For e-commerce operational flows, Stripe and Shopify Payments net consumer card transactions in EUR and payout to the principal IBAN; when USD/GBP wallets are enabled, direct funds to the bank's multi-currency sub-account or an EMI, then execute a same-day bank FX swap rather than accepting on-platform conversion spreads. Reconcile PSP settlement reports, chargebacks and refunds to the bank statement daily.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for onshore-CNY-denominated supplier contracts
EUR/USD FX swaps (tom-next and spot/forward) for liquidity and cash sweeping
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for long-term asset-liability hedging of significant USD trade debt or receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and annual report filing (déclaration de dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through Luxembourg Business Registers / eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year end: shareholders' meeting must approve annual accounts within 6 months; filing with RCS must occur within 1 month after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes managers to administrative fines; persistent default after formal warning triggers RCS strike-off (radiation) proceedings and potential criminal sanctions for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and update of RBE registry (déclaration d'actualisation du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers / eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership; if no change, annual no-change confirmation within 1 month after the anniversary of the RBE registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declarations may lead to criminal fines, imprisonment of managers, and administrative strike-off for continued violation of RBE filing obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is required for a Luxembourg SARL if at least two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above €4,400,000; net turnover above €8,800,000; average workforce above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and the amended Companies Law; IFRS is permitted for individual financial statements of certain entities and mandatory for listed groups and regulated financial institutions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file any modification to the beneficial ownership data with the RBE within 30 days. When no modification occurs, an annual no-change confirmation must be lodged within the calendar year covering the anniversary of the initial RBE registration, attesting the ongoing accuracy of the registered information.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,300 - 2,800 per year depending on domiciliation services and corporate agent requirements
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 15,000 for a small-to-mid-size SARL when a statutory or shareholder-requested audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + municipal business tax (6.75% in Luxembourg City); aggregate headline rate up to 24.94%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Preferential regimes: 80% IP income exemption (IP box), participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (effective 0%), 8% investment tax credit, notional interest deduction on new equity, and horizontal group consolidation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite for post-2017 losses; annual offset of losses above EUR 1 million limited to 90% of taxable income)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Luxembourg Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via eTADE (e-Tax Administration portal, tax.lu).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by 31 May of the year following the closure of the financial year; extension to 31 December may be obtained through eTADE. For a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is therefore 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification and registration: name, legal form, Luxembourg RCS number, registered office, principal ISIC/NAICS activity (e.g., 4791 retail of smart home IoT hardware).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company filing due to a Luxembourg permanent establishment, identify the PE's local address, RCS registration, and designated Luxembourg fiscal representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period, year-end date, reporting currency and accounting basis (LUX GAAP).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert accounts to EUR using the ECB reference rate; attach the PE's separate or deemed balance sheet and tax reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: commercial profit, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax adjustments and loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Luxembourg-source income attributable to the PE; exclude foreign income covered by an applicable double tax treaty and attach the relevant exemption/progression statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax credits: DTA relief, foreign withholding tax credits, investment tax credits, and advance income tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a valid foreign tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty partner and use Form 290 to recover excess withholding tax on Luxembourg-source dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the final tax due, monthly default interest of 0.6%, and possible 20% ex-officio assessment uplift. Criminal fines and director liability apply for fraudulent non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% at source, reduced to 0% for qualifying intra-EU subsidiaries under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive; treaty rates generally 5%, 10% or 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must deliver to the Luxembourg paying agent a foreign tax residence certificate (TRC) meeting the DTA requirements, together with a Form 290 refund/clearance application where the reduced rate is applied post-withholding. The paying agent must verify entitlement before distribution; otherwise 15% is withheld and the excess can be reclaimed via the Luxembourg direct tax refund procedure within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: 0% withholding tax on interest and royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-residents; under tax treaties the rate remains 0%; anti-abuse rules may recharacterize abusive payments as dividends subject to 15% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750 million (consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent triggering mandatory Master File and Local File duties under EU administrative cooperation framework); otherwise documentation must still be contemporaneously maintained upon a specific request from Luxembourg tax authorities under Art. 56bis LIR.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) similar to offshore centers, but substance must be present under the OECD/BEPS nexus approach, ATAD general anti-abuse rule, and the Luxembourg tax administration's substance doctrine; the SARL must prove real premises, employees, management presence and business activity in Luxembourg to be resident, avoid CFC/GAAR challenges and retain treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of e-commerce sales revenue, fabrication of purchase invoices, use of fictitious or shell suppliers for smart home IoT hardware, or concealment of Stripe/Shopify payments from the annual CIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment with 100% penalty for bad faith, 10% late filing surcharge, monthly interest 0.6%, and criminal prosecution under the Luxembourg Criminal Code and direct tax law: imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the tax underpaid; courts may order travel bans, seizure of passports and personal assets, and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sale of IoT hardware components to a related trading company in a low-tax jurisdiction at a 90% markup, stripping profit from the Luxembourg SARL without operational substance and without a transfer pricing study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may adjust the profit to arm's length, apply 25% administrative fine on the reassessment, and impose the EUR 1,000,000 CbCR penalty if documentation is missing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In cases of intentional transfer pricing misstatement, directors may be held personally accountable for the incremental assessed taxes and fines; an international arrest warrant or travel ban may be issued under a Grand-Ducal extradition process for serious tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SARL as a mere letterbox entity, with no office, staff, or management functions in Luxembourg, to channel IoT retail profits and claim treaty benefits on outbound dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under LOB/PPT rules, reclassification of the company as tax-transparent, disallowance of loss carry-forwards, and net wealth tax minimum assessments; criminal anti-shell fines up to EUR 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficiaries face piercing of the corporate veil under the principle of simulation: civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 1 year for knowingly misleading tax authorities under the Luxembourg Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing the origin of funds by processing smart home IoT sales through cash-intensive intermediary companies without KYC/AML controls, while failing to file suspicious transaction reports to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF sanctions for AML violations: fines up to EUR 1 million or 5% of annual turnover for legal persons; confiscation of proceeds and enhancement of tax penalties to 200%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual liability of compliance officers and directors under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004: imprisonment up to 5 years, personal fines, and travel bans; passports may be withdrawn pending criminal proceedings.
